title: S3 Versioning, Lifecycle & Replication 🔄
description: Advanced features to protect, manage, and duplicate your data automatically.

slides.title: Versioning: Undelete Everything ♻️
slides.content:
# Keep Every Variant

Enabling versioning on a bucket means S3 keeps all versions of an object, including deleted ones (just adds a delete marker).

- If you overwrite an object, the old version remains recoverable.
- If you delete an object, you can delete the delete marker to restore it.
- Once enabled, versioning **cannot be disabled** – only suspended.
- You can use **MFA Delete** for extra protection against accidental deletion.

Use versioning to protect against both accidental and malicious deletions.

quizData.question: You delete an object in a versioned bucket. What happens?

options.text: A delete marker is added, and the object can be restored
The object is moved to Glacier

quizData.explanation: A simple DELETE in a versioned bucket adds a delete marker, hiding the object. To permanently delete, you must specify the version ID.

slides.title: Lifecycle Management: Move Data Automatically 🔁
slides.content:
# Transition and Expiration Rules

S3 Lifecycle policies let you automatically move objects between storage classes or delete them based on age.

- **Transition actions**: e.g., move objects to S3 Standard‑IA after 30 days, then to Glacier after 90 days.
- **Expiration actions**: delete old versions or incomplete multipart uploads.
- You can create rules per prefix or tag.

This optimises cost: frequently accessed data stays on fast, expensive storage; old data moves to cheap archive.

slides.title: S3 Storage Classes 💰
slides.content:
# Choose Based on Access Pattern

- **S3 Standard**: frequent access, low latency, high durability.
- **S3 Intelligent‑Tiering**: auto‑moves objects between frequent and infrequent tiers based on usage (small monitoring fee).
- **S3 Standard‑IA (Infrequent Access)**: lower storage cost, retrieval fee.
- **S3 One Zone‑IA**: like IA but data stored in a single AZ (less durable, cheaper).
- **S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval**: archive with millisecond retrieval.
- **S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval**: minutes to hours retrieval, very cheap.
- **S3 Glacier Deep Archive**: lowest cost, 12‑hour retrieval time.

Lifecycle policies leverage these classes.

quizData.question: You have log data that is rarely accessed, but when needed it must be retrieved within 5 minutes. Which storage class is appropriate?
quizData.explanation: Standard‑IA offers millisecond retrieval and is for infrequent access. Glacier has retrieval delays.

slides.title: Cross‑Region Replication (CRR) ↔️
slides.content:
# Disaster Recovery & Compliance

You can automatically replicate objects from one bucket to another in a different region.
- Requires versioning enabled on both source and destination.
- You can replicate all objects or a subset by prefix/tag.
- Can use **Same‑Region Replication (SRR)** for log aggregation or compliance.
- Replication is asynchronous; eventual consistency (within minutes usually).

Use cases: meet compliance, reduce latency for global users, backup.
